description: USE ROLE and USE SECONDARY ROLES - switching the session's PRIMARY role, which CURRENT_ROLE() reflects, and adjusting the secondary ones, with existence validation. A role can only be ACTIVATED by a user it has been GRANTED to: live-verified, without the grant the statement fails 'Requested role ANALYST is not assigned to the executing user. Specify another role to activate.' The working spelling is GRANT ROLE <role> TO USER <user>, and live REJECTS GRANT ROLE r TO USER IDENTIFIER(CURRENT_USER()) with a syntax error at the parenthesis - so the executing user's name has to be READ FIRST and spliced into the statement, which the converted test does through a scripting block and EXECUTE IMMEDIATE rather than through host-language string building. The account is stateful across runs, so everything is created tolerantly and handed back at the end, and the session steps OFF a role before dropping it, since a session left on a dropped role has none. The system roles switch without any grant, a nonexistent role is refused, and USE SECONDARY ROLES ALL then NONE adjust the active set without error. Converted 1:1 from security/UseRoleTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS analyst

DECLARE u VARCHAR; BEGIN u := (SELECT CURRENT_USER()); EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS "' || :u || '"'; EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT ROLE analyst TO USER "' || :u || '"'; RETURN 'granted'; END
DECLARE u VARCHAR; BEGIN u := (SELECT CURRENT_USER()); EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'REVOKE ROLE analyst FROM USER "' || :u || '"'; RETURN 'revoked'; END
CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS r1
